channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Nicotine Pouches Are Not Cigarettes. Regulation Should Reflect the Difference
item.description: A nicotine pouch is not a cigarette without smoke; it is a different product category altogether. That distinction matters for regulation, because rules designed around combustion do not automatically make sense for oral, smoke-free nicotine. Pouches still need standards, age controls and monitoring, but policy should reflect their actual risk profile rather than the stigma attached to cigarettes. Regulation is most credible when it recognises differences instead of flattening them. (Published on August 03, 2026byvapingpost.com)

item.title: Two Presentations, One Crisis: When the Evidence Points Beyond Enforcement
item.description: Two presentations can reveal one crisis when the same evidence points are interpreted in opposite ways. In nicotine policy, that crisis is not only about disagreement — it is about whether science is being used to clarify risk or to defend existing positions. When data on safer products is filtered through ideology, smokers may be left with confusion instead of useful guidance. Public health needs evidence that informs decisions, not evidence selected to protect a narrative. (Published on August 03, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Which Nicotine Pouch Formula Stays More Stable? | #GFN26ScienceLab
item.description: Stability may sound like a technical detail, but it shapes whether a nicotine pouch performs consistently over time. Formula design can affect nicotine release, shelf life, user experience and the standards regulators should expect from smoke-free products. That makes product chemistry part of the public health conversation, not just a manufacturing issue. If nicotine pouches are to be regulated responsibly, evidence on formulation and stability should matter as much as assumptions about the category. (Published on August 04, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: "My Best Friend"
item.description: Sometimes harm reduction begins with one person who refuses to give up on someone else. Behind the evidence, policy arguments and product categories are people who smoke, people who love them, and people trying to keep them alive long enough to find a safer path. Tobacco harm reduction is often discussed as a technical issue, but its urgency is deeply human. The goal is not to win an argument about nicotine — it is to reduce harm for real people. (Published on August 04, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: TAM: Ottawa's proposed vape flavour ban ignores science and punishes 2 million adult Canadians
item.description: Two million adult Canadians should not become collateral damage in a policy designed around fear. Ottawa’s proposed vape flavour ban risks removing the products that many adults rely on to stay away from cigarettes. Science should guide regulation: protect young people through enforcement and age controls, but do not erase the flavours that help make switching work. A policy that punishes adult smokers for choosing a lower-risk option is not harm reduction. (Published on August 04, 2026bywesternstandard.news)
